question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` expose internal OpenClaw tool telemetry, and if yes, should it be a redacted opt-in trace surface rather than OpenAI `tool_calls`?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally describe `tool_calls` as caller-supplied client tools, while internal tool arguments are security-sensitive and prior built-in telemetry PRs were not accepted.

options.title: Keep client-tool-only
options.body: Document that Chat Completions `tool_calls` are only for caller-supplied tools and route internal execution visibility to audit, trajectory, or Gateway protocol surfaces.

options.title: Design redacted opt-in telemetry
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved API/config contract for internal tool traces with explicit redaction, scopes, and compatibility tests before implementation.

options.title: Expose internals as tool_calls
options.body: Return internal tools as OpenAI `tool_calls`, accepting the risk that already-executed audit events may look like caller-executable function calls.

recommendation.title: Keep client-tool-only
recommendation.body: Document that Chat Completions `tool_calls` are only for caller-supplied tools and route internal execution visibility to audit, trajectory, or Gateway protocol surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and followed up on the current Chat Completions tool protocol, making them the best available routing owner for this API-shape decision.
